lines.trans: Push down with the heel of your hand, Peng, fold once, turn halfway, push again!
Got it, chef! How does the dough look now?
Smooth and soft, and springing right back—into the warm bowl under a damp cloth!
Four egg yolks, fresh lemon juice, and three spoons of sugar from the sugar jar, Mei!
Keep whisking over low heat, Qing—never let the bottom of the pot boil!

words.gloss: by all means; whatever you do

lines.trans: How is your ankle feeling this morning, Mei?
Honestly? Half the swelling is gone already thanks to you two keeping me off my feet!

words.gloss: step on the ground; get off one's feet

lines.trans: Look how thick and glossy the golden lemon curd just turned!
Turn off the flame right away! Stir in one cold cube of unsalted butter!
Smell that bright lemon steam—the whole ground floor is filled with fragrance!
Twenty crisp almond tart shells are lined up ready on the cooling rack!
Not bad at all, apprentices—my bakery is in safe hands with you!

meanings.note: Pinyin: yī. Changes tone to yí before 4th tone (一个 yí gè) and yì before 1st/2nd/3rd tones (一杯 yì bēi).

examples.text: 第一天上班，我走得快。电脑在哪里？
examples.trans: On my first day at work, I walk fast. Where is the computer?

examples.text: 第一条规矩：先喝热茶，再去开门。
examples.trans: Rule number one: drink hot tea first, then go answer the door.

meanings.note: Pinyin: yí bàn. Combines 一 ('one') + 半 ('half'); note yī shifts to yí before 4th-tone bàn.

examples.text: 这壶热茶我们已经喝了一半。
examples.trans: We have already drunk half of this pot of hot tea.

examples.text: 第二页乐谱有一半还没有写完。
examples.trans: Half of the second page of sheet music is still unfinished.

meanings.note: Locative noun yīlóu ('first floor').

examples.text: 一楼的碎玻璃都已经修过了。
examples.trans: The broken glass on the first floor has already been fixed.

examples.text: 前台接待处就在一楼大厅。
examples.trans: The reception desk is right in the first-floor lobby.

meanings.note: Pinyin: sān. Cardinal number 3; combines with measure words (三个) and floors (三楼).

examples.text: 不在，只有我的笔和三张旧收据！
examples.trans: Not there—only my pen and three old receipts!

examples.text: 三瓶牛奶、二十个鸡蛋、黄油、奶酪和红苹果！
examples.trans: Three bottles of milk, twenty eggs, butter, cheese, and red apples!

meanings.note: Pinyin: shàng. Used both as a directional verb/complement ('up, onto') and location word ('on top of').

examples.text: 早上好。没锁，先把把手往上提，再推。
examples.trans: Good morning. Not locked; lift the handle up first, then push.

examples.text: 就在您额头上，安全得很。
examples.trans: Right there on your forehead, completely safe.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xià. Used for downward motion ('go down'), location ('under'), or 'next' (下周).

examples.text: 那是什么铃声？有人按了两下！
examples.trans: What was that bell sound? Somebody rang twice!

examples.text: 就算四号房空着，旧电线也会响两下。
examples.trans: Even when room four is empty, the old wire still rings twice.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xià qù. Compound directional complement 下 ('down') + 去 ('away from speaker'), often attached after action verbs like 按下去 ('press down').

examples.text: 把开关轻轻按下去，走廊的灯就亮了。
examples.trans: Press the switch gently down and the hallway light comes on.

examples.text: 如果雨一直下下去，我们就在屋里喝茶。
examples.trans: If the rain keeps coming down, we will drink tea indoors.

下地.gloss: get out of bed; step on the ground

meanings.en: get out of bed; step on the ground
meanings.note: Pinyin: xià dì. Separable verb-object compound 下 ('step down onto') + 地 ('ground/floor'), often used when recovering from an injury or illness.

examples.text: 多亏你们俩不让我下地，我的脚踝已经消肿一半了。
examples.trans: Thanks to you two not letting me step on the ground, my ankle has already gone down by half.

examples.text: 医生叮嘱她先在椅子上休息两天，暂时不要下地走路。
examples.trans: The doctor advised her to rest in a chair for two days and not put weight on her foot yet.

meanings.note: Pinyin: bù. Standard negation for present/future/habitual verbs and adjectives; shifts to bú before a 4th tone (不是 bú shì).

examples.text: 停电的时候，纸还能用。
examples.trans: Paper still works when the power goes out.

examples.text: 我要看预订本子，可是找不到我的眼镜了！
examples.trans: I need to read the booking ledger, yet I cannot find my glasses!

examples.text: 我觉得我跟他离得好远，他跟我说一句话，我脑子就直接充血，使劲转不停。
examples.trans: Yet he feels so far away — when he speaks one sentence to me, the blood rushes to my head and my mind spins!

examples.text: 这件事我们再商量一下。
examples.trans: Let's discuss this matter a bit more.

meanings.note: Pinyin: bú cuò. Warm everyday praise meaning 'really quite good!'.

examples.text: 第二天上班，干得不错，新手。
examples.trans: For day two on the job, nicely done, rookie.

examples.text: 这家小店的红茶味道真不错。
examples.trans: The black tea at this little shop tastes really good.

meanings.note: Pinyin: liǎng. Used instead of 二 when counting things with a measure word (两个, 两把, 两间).

examples.text: 那是什么铃声？有人按了两下！
examples.trans: What was that bell sound? Somebody rang twice!

examples.text: 就算四号房空着，旧电线也会响两下。
examples.trans: Even when room four is empty, the old wire still rings twice.

meanings.note: Pinyin: gè. Most common Mandarin measure word (量词), placed between a number/demonstrative and a noun (一个人, 这个).

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 刚烤好的面包卷！趁热拿一个吧。
examples.trans: Freshly baked bread rolls! Take one while it is hot.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhǔ chú. Combines 主 ('chief/head') + 厨 ('cook/kitchen'); measure word: 位 (wèi).

examples.text: 小美主厨坐在两个枕头上，用木勺指挥整个厨房。
examples.trans: Head Chef Mei sat propped on two pillows, directing the whole kitchen with a wooden spoon.

examples.text: 这位年轻的主厨最擅长烤酥脆的杏仁柠檬挞。
examples.trans: This young head chef specializes in baking crisp almond lemon tarts.

meanings.note: Pinyin: yě. Always stands directly before the verb or adjective, never at the end of a clause.

examples.text: 就算四号房空着，旧电线也会响两下。
examples.trans: Even when room four is empty, the old wire still rings twice.

examples.text: 周经理早！桌子很干净，钥匙也准备好了。
examples.trans: Morning, Manager Zhou! The desk is clean, and the keys are ready too.

meanings.note: Pinyin: le. After a verb, marks completion; at the end of a sentence, signals a change of situation.

examples.text: 早上好！请问，门锁了吗？
examples.trans: Good morning! Excuse me, is the door locked?

examples.text: 啊，开了！谢谢。我是小晴，新来的前台。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Qing, the new receptionist.

meanings.note: Two tens: èrshí.

examples.text: 他二十岁了。
examples.trans: He is twenty years old.

examples.text: 看了二十年电视。
examples.trans: Watched television for twenty years.

examples.text: 这是交给啊。
examples.trans: This is hand over to.

examples.text: 那个交给好。
examples.trans: That hand over to is good.

meanings.note: Pinyin: liàng. Describes bright light or a surface polished clean (擦亮 'polish bright').

examples.text: 隔壁的小洗手间呢？灯亮吗？
examples.trans: What about the small bathroom next door? Does the light work?

examples.text: 火苗亮了——稳稳的蓝火，正合适。
examples.trans: The flame is lit—steady blue fire, right as it should be.

meanings.note: Pinyin: jīn tiān. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 今天一天 ('all day today').

examples.text: 对，八间客房，八把铜钥匙。四号房的客人今天到。
examples.trans: Yes, eight rooms, eight brass keys. Room four's guest arrives today.

examples.text: 今天四号房的客人住一整个星期，一定要完美！
examples.trans: Today's guest in room four is staying a whole week; everything must be perfect!

meanings.note: Pinyin: wèi. Polite counterpart of 个 when counting guests, customers, or teachers (一位客人, 这位老师).

examples.text: 太谢谢你们两位了。
examples.trans: Thank you both so very much.

examples.text: 七点半有八位饿肚子的客人下楼啊！
examples.trans: At seven thirty, eight hungry guests are coming downstairs!

meanings.note: Pinyin: nǐ. Everyday singular 'you' among colleagues, friends, and peers; use 您 for polite respect.

examples.text: 我叫老陈。你早到了十分钟。
examples.trans: I'm called Chen. You arrived ten minutes early.

examples.text: 你好！你就是小晴吧？我是厨房的小美。
examples.trans: Hello! You must be Qing, right? I am Mei from the kitchen.

meanings.note: Pinyin: nǐ men. Plural 'you' for addressing two or more people (including polite groups).

examples.text: 太谢谢你们两位了。
examples.trans: Thank you both so very much.

examples.text: 不怪你们。只是我身上只有这件外套！
examples.trans: It is not your fault. Still, I only have this one coat on me!

meanings.note: Pinyin: liǎ. Colloquial fusion of 两个, never followed by 个 (我们俩 'the two of us').

examples.text: 啊！黄色柠檬糖霜——每个星期五我们俩都抢边角那一块！
examples.trans: Oh! Yellow lemon glaze—every single Friday the two of us fought over the corner piece!

examples.text: 别动，你们俩。听到路边汽车停下的声音了吗？
examples.trans: Hold still, both of you. Hear that car engine stopping at the curb?

meanings.note: Pinyin: guāng huá. Combines 光 ('polished/sleek') + 滑 ('smooth'); often paired in 又光滑又柔软 ('both smooth and supple').

examples.text: 揉好的面团表面又光滑又柔软，按下去马上弹回来。
examples.trans: The kneaded dough is both smooth and supple on the surface, springing right back when pressed.

examples.text: 打磨过的核桃木桌面摸起来非常光滑。
examples.trans: The sanded walnut tabletop feels wonderfully smooth to the touch.

meanings.note: Pinyin: guān. Used for closing doors/windows and turning off lights, taps, or valves.

examples.text: 拿稳了！你已经关掉总水阀了吗？
examples.trans: Steady! Did you turn off the main water valve already?

examples.text: 关掉了，水也放空了。把左边那把重扳手递给我。
examples.trans: Turned off and drained. Pass me that heavy wrench on your left.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zài. Marks a next step in sequence (先提再推) or a future repetition (再见 'see you again').

examples.text: 早上好。没锁，先把把手往上提，再推。
examples.trans: Good morning. Not locked; lift the handle up first, then push.

examples.text: 第一条规矩：先喝热茶，再去开门。
examples.trans: Rule number one: drink hot tea first, then go answer the door.

meanings.note: Pinyin: bīng. Measure word (量词): 块 (kuài), e.g. 一块冰 ('a piece of ice').

examples.text: 别担心！用冰气泡水一擦，橙汁就掉。
examples.trans: Do not worry! Wipe it once with cold sparkling water and orange juice comes right out.

examples.text: 杯子里加了两块冰。
examples.trans: Two ice cubes were added to the glass.

related.gloss: a piece of ice (measure word 块)

meanings.note: Pinyin: bié. Most commonly means 'do not' in polite commands (别担心 'don't worry'); as a verb, 'pin/clip on'.

examples.text: 谁也别说出去！门铃响的时候要微笑。
examples.trans: Do not tell anyone! Smile warmly when the bell rings.

examples.text: 您先坐下，别着急，我们马上看行李牌。
examples.trans: Please sit down first and do not worry; we will check the luggage tag right away.

meanings.note: Pinyin: sháo. Used both as a noun (勺子 'spoon') and as a measure word for spoonfuls (一勺蜂蜜 'a spoonful of honey').

examples.text: 喝热柠檬茶的时候，加一勺蜂蜜最香。
examples.trans: Hot lemon tea smells best when you add a spoonful of honey.

examples.text: 请给我拿一把干净的小木勺。
examples.trans: Please bring me a clean little wooden spoon.

meanings.en: by all means; be sure (not) to
meanings.note: Pinyin: qiān wàn. Strong, caring emphasis before 别 or 要 (千万别忘 'whatever you do, don't forget').

examples.text: 我还没喝早咖啡呢，千万别说急事！
examples.trans: I have not had my morning coffee yet; please do not say emergency!

examples.text: 小美，千万别因为我们多忙活。
examples.trans: Mei, please do not go to extra trouble on our account.

meanings.note: Pinyin: bàn. Follows a measure word for 'and a half' (七点半 '7:30') or precedes a measure word for 'half a' (半个小时).

examples.text: 给您四号钥匙。早餐从七点半到十点。
examples.trans: Here is key number four for you. Breakfast is from seven thirty to ten.

examples.text: 七点半有八位饿肚子的客人下楼啊！
examples.trans: At seven thirty, eight hungry guests are coming downstairs!

meanings.note: Pinyin: yòu. Marks an action repeating, or pairs two qualities in 又A又B ('both A and B').

examples.text: 真的可以吗？看着又好看又暖和！
examples.trans: Is that really alright? It looks both lovely and warm!

examples.text: 又是深蓝色行李箱！这是宋老师的吗？
examples.trans: Another dark-blue suitcase! Is this Teacher Song's?

examples.text: 如果你是个富人的话，你会让自己变得更好。
examples.trans: And if you are wealthy, you push yourself to become a better person.

examples.text: 这些人也太夸张了吧，变得太极端了吧！
examples.trans: These people are outrageous — talk about a complete one-eighty!

meanings.note: Pinyin: ya. Gentle exclamation of surprise or realization.

examples.text: 因为好咖啡和热面包让人开心呀！
examples.trans: Because good coffee and warm bread make people happy!

examples.text: 呀，这就是星期一火车上那只双胞胎箱子吗？
examples.trans: Oh, is this that twin suitcase from Monday's train?

meanings.note: Pinyin: sì. Cardinal number 4.

examples.text: 对，八间客房，八把铜钥匙。四号房的客人今天到。
examples.trans: Yes, eight rooms, eight brass keys. Room four's guest arrives today.

examples.text: 那里没人。那是四号房的门铃。
examples.trans: Nobody is there. That is the buzzer from room four.

meanings.note: Pinyin: huí tóu. Appears in the friendly farewell 回头见！ ('See you soon!').

examples.text: 我先去送热茶，我们回头聊！
examples.trans: Let me deliver this hot tea first—we will talk soon!

examples.text: 今天辛苦了，回头见！
examples.trans: Great work today—see you soon!

meanings.note: Pinyin: huí lái. Directional compound for returning toward the speaker's place.

examples.text: 一点没破！是谁送回来的？
examples.trans: Not cracked at all! Who brought it back?

examples.text: 付了现金！打开工具箱等我，我往桥那边跑回来了！
examples.trans: Paid in cash! Open your toolbox and wait—I am running back across the bridge!

meanings.note: Pinyin: quān. Counts full turns of a key, wrench, or lap around a block (一圈 'one full turn').

examples.text: 一圈，两圈……看新铜螺纹咬合得多干净。
examples.trans: One turn, two turns... look how cleanly the new brass thread fits.

examples.text: 我绕着广场走了一圈。
examples.trans: I walked one lap around the square.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zài. As main verb/preposition, gives location (在院子里); before another verb, marks ongoing action ('be doing').

examples.text: 第一天上班，我走得快。电脑在哪里？
examples.trans: On my first day at work, I walk fast. Where is the computer?

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

meanings.note: Pinyin: de. Neutral-tone structural particle turning a descriptive phrase into an adverb before a verb (轻轻地放 'set down gently'); distinct from noun di4 ('ground').

examples.text: 小晴整整齐齐地把茶杯排在木架上。
examples.trans: Qing arranged the teacups neatly on the wooden shelf.

examples.text: 老陈仔细地检查了每一根新电线。
examples.trans: Chen carefully checked every single new wire.

块.gloss: measure word for pieces and yuan

meanings.en: measure word for pieces and yuan
meanings.note: Pinyin: kuài. Counts chunks/pieces (一块蛋糕 'a piece of cake') and spoken yuan of money (五块钱 'five yuan').

examples.text: 钱箱里拿五十块，记得要收据！
examples.trans: Here is fifty yuan from the cash box; remember to get a receipt!

examples.text: 在这儿！一共三十八块，找回十二块零钱。
examples.trans: Right here! Thirty-eight yuan in total, with twelve yuan back in change.

meanings.note: Pinyin: duō. Means 'many' as an adjective, 'how…?' before adjectives (多大), or 'more than' after round numbers (三十多).

examples.text: 声音轻，很有礼貌，大概三十多岁，有点紧张。
examples.trans: Soft-spoken, very polite, around thirty-something, and a bit nervous.

examples.text: 说实话，我比以前灰色办公室喜欢这儿多了。
examples.trans: Honestly, I like this place far better than my old grey office.

meanings.note: Pinyin: duō kuī. Gives warm credit for avoiding trouble.

examples.text: 这一周的街道记录全在里面，多亏了你。
examples.trans: All my street notes from this week are inside—thanks to you.

examples.text: 多亏你提醒我，差点忘了拿钥匙。
examples.trans: Thanks to your reminder, I nearly forgot to grab my keys.

meanings.note: Pinyin: hǎo. Main adjective 'good'; as a result complement after a verb, means 'ready/completed properly' (修好, 准备好).

examples.text: 早上好！请问，门锁了吗？
examples.trans: Good morning! Excuse me, is the door locked?

examples.text: 早上好。没锁，先把把手往上提，再推。
examples.trans: Good morning. Not locked; lift the handle up first, then push.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xiǎo. Everyday adjective for small size; also prefixes younger colleagues' names warmly (小晴, 小美).

examples.text: 早上好，姑娘。我有一个宋名下的预订。
examples.trans: Good morning, young lady. I have a booking for Song.

examples.text: 白纸包着什么？一个木头小火车！
examples.trans: What is wrapped in white paper? A little wooden train!

meanings.note: Pinyin: yǐ jīng. Often pairs with sentence-final 了 (已经到了 'has already arrived').

examples.text: 没错！你已经很习惯这儿了。
examples.trans: Exactly! You already fit right in here.

examples.text: 还好烤箱里的面团已经放进去了。
examples.trans: My dough is already in the oven, at least.

meanings.note: Pinyin: bù. Measure word (量词): 块 (kuài), e.g. 一块布 ('a piece of cloth').

examples.text: 周经理，给您干净布和冷水。
examples.trans: Manager Zhou, here is a clean cloth and cold water for you.

examples.text: 请拿一块干净的布擦桌子。
examples.trans: Please take a clean cloth to wipe the table.

related.gloss: a piece of cloth (measure word 块)

meanings.note: Pinyin: kāi. Versatile verb for opening doors, starting business, turning on taps/lights, or water boiling.

examples.text: 啊，开了！谢谢。我是小晴，新来的前台。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Qing, the new receptionist.

examples.text: 当然不能偷看……咦，自己翻开在中间那页了！
examples.trans: Of course we must not peek... oh, it fell open to the middle page by itself!

meanings.note: Pinyin: tán. Used for playing the piano or guitar (弹钢琴 'play the piano').

examples.text: 那里住着一位老木匠和两个孙子——哥哥弹钢琴，弟弟最爱小火车！
examples.trans: An old carpenter lived there with two grandsons—the older brother played piano, and the younger loved toy trains!

examples.text: 哥哥性格爽朗声音大，弹音阶总是急匆匆的。
examples.trans: The older brother was bold and loud, always rushing through his scales.

meanings.note: Pinyin: wǎng. Guides movement in directions (往上提 'lift upward', 往左拐 'turn left').

examples.text: 早上好。没锁，先把把手往上提，再推。
examples.trans: Good morning. Not locked; lift the handle up first, then push.

examples.text: 从这儿往里走。我帮您把蓝色行李箱提上去。
examples.trans: Walk inward from here. I will carry the blue suitcase up for you.

meanings.note: Pinyin: tú dì. Combines 徒 ('follower/apprentice') + 弟 ('junior/younger brother'); pairs with 师父 ('master craftsperson'); measure word: 位 (wèi) or 个 (gè).

examples.text: 小美满意地点点头说：“两位徒弟，我的面包房交给你们放心了！”
examples.trans: Mei nodded with satisfaction and said, 'Apprentices, I can trust my bakery to the two of you!'

examples.text: 志鹏跟着小美当了一天徒弟，已经学会了怎么揉光滑的面团。
examples.trans: After spending a day as Mei's apprentice, Peng has already learned how to knead smooth bread dough.

meanings.note: Pinyin: kuài. As an adjective/adverb, 'fast/quickly'; in 快…了, 'about to'.

examples.text: 第一天上班，我走得快。电脑在哪里？
examples.trans: On my first day at work, I walk fast. Where is the computer?

examples.text: 小晴，快看里面！这不是我的箱子！
examples.trans: Qing, look inside quickly! This is not my case!

meanings.note: Pinyin: zěn me yàng. Asks for an opinion or update on how things are going.

examples.text: 怎么样？他发火了吗？要退钱吗？
examples.trans: How did it go? Did he lose his temper? Did he ask for a refund?

examples.text: 小晴，今天我的领带怎么样？一滴橙汁都没有！
examples.trans: Qing, how does my tie look today? Not a single drop of orange juice!

examples.text: 实习感觉怎么样？
examples.trans: How does the internship feel?

examples.text: 这是感觉。
examples.trans: This is 感觉.

meanings.note: Pinyin: wǒ. First-person singular pronoun; add 的 for 'my' (我的) and 们 for 'we/us' (我们).

examples.text: 啊，开了！谢谢。我是小晴，新来的前台。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Qing, the new receptionist.

examples.text: 我叫老陈。你早到了十分钟。
examples.trans: I'm called Chen. You arrived ten minutes early.

meanings.note: Pinyin: shǒu zhǎng. Combines 手 ('hand') + 掌 ('palm/flat pad of the hand'); 手掌根 refers to the heel of the palm used in kneading dough.

examples.text: 揉面的时候要用手掌根往下推，折一次，转半圈。
examples.trans: When kneading dough, push down with the heel of your palm, fold once, and turn half a circle.

examples.text: 刚出炉的热茶杯握在手掌里，暖和极了。
examples.trans: Holding a freshly poured warm teacup in the palm of your hand feels wonderfully cozy.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhé. Used for folding chairs, blueprints, or paper.

examples.text: 等等，换房间我们给他打多少折？
examples.trans: Wait—what discount do we offer him for changing rooms?

examples.text: 快把那张纸折起来，塞进口袋里。
examples.trans: Fold up that sheet of paper right now and tuck it into your pocket.

meanings.note: Pinyin: àn. Used for pressing a doorbell, elevator button, or key (按门铃).

examples.text: 那是什么铃声？有人按了两下！
examples.trans: What was that bell sound? Somebody rang twice!

examples.text: 宋老师，怎么了？您按了门铃！
examples.trans: Teacher Song, what happened? You rang the bell!

meanings.note: Pinyin: tà dǐ. Combines 挞 ('tart') + 底 ('base/crust').

examples.text: 用烤香的杏仁粉做的挞底既酥脆又香甜。
examples.trans: A tart crust made with toasted almond flour is crisp and fragrant.

examples.text: 把挞底烤成金黄色以后，再填入柠檬酱。
examples.trans: Bake the tart shell until golden, then fill it with lemon curd.

meanings.note: Pinyin: pái. Counts rows of keys, seats, or houses (一排钥匙 'a row of keys').

examples.text: 等星期五中午箱子主人进来，我一定坐第一排看！
examples.trans: When the suitcase owner walks in Friday at noon, I am sitting in the front row!

examples.text: 墙上整整齐齐挂着一排钥匙。
examples.trans: A neat row of keys hangs on the wall.

meanings.note: Pinyin: tuī. Opposite of 拉 ('pull'); used for pushing doors open.

examples.text: 早上好。没锁，先把把手往上提，再推。
examples.trans: Good morning. Not locked; lift the handle up first, then push.

examples.text: 这扇木门往里推就开了。
examples.trans: Push this wooden door inward and it opens.

meanings.note: Pinyin: jiǎo. Action verb for stirring liquids, sauces, or batters with a spoon or whisk.

examples.text: 小晴开着小火不停地搅，不让锅底的柠檬酱煮开。
examples.trans: Qing stirred nonstop over low heat so the lemon curd at the bottom of the pot wouldn't boil.

examples.text: 喝热红茶的时候，他喜欢放一小勺蜂蜜轻轻搅一下。
examples.trans: When drinking hot black tea, he likes adding a small spoonful of honey and giving it a gentle stir.

meanings.note: Pinyin: jiǎo yún. Resultative verb compound 搅 ('stir') + 匀 ('even/uniform'), used when blending butter, sugar, or seasonings thoroughly into a mixture.

examples.text: 关火以后马上放一块冰的无盐黄油进去搅匀！
examples.trans: Right after turning off the heat, drop in a cube of cold unsalted butter and stir until smooth!

examples.text: 先把蛋黄和柠檬汁在碗里搅匀，再倒进温热的锅里。
examples.trans: Whisk the egg yolks and lemon juice until smooth in a bowl first, then pour them into the warm pot.

meanings.note: Verb shōudào ('received; radio/workplace "copy that"').

examples.text: 收到，我们会继续盯着直播。
examples.trans: Copy that; we will keep watching the live feed.

examples.text: 我已经收到你发的邮件了。
examples.trans: I have received the email you sent.

meanings.note: Pinyin: fàng. Everyday verb for placing an object somewhere (放在桌子上).

examples.text: 我们不知道。有人放在台阶上，按了门铃。
examples.trans: We do not know. Someone set it on the step and rang the bell.

examples.text: 小勺子和餐巾放在哪里？
examples.trans: Where do the small spoons and napkins go?

related.gloss: handle with care (lift gently, set down gently)

meanings.note: Pinyin: fàng xīn. Literally 'set one's heart down' (请放心 'rest assured!').

examples.text: 放心吧，周经理。房间干净，毛巾也是新的。
examples.trans: Relax, Manager Zhou. The room is clean, and the towels are fresh.

examples.text: 放心吧，老陈，我们替你保密！
examples.trans: Rest assured, Chen—we will keep your secret!

related.gloss: handle with care (lift gently, set down gently)

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhěng gè. Combines 整 ('whole') + 个; modifies singular nouns directly without another measure word (整个中央八度).

examples.text: 修好那根琴槌以后，宋老师给整个中央八度调了音。
examples.trans: After fixing that hammer, Teacher Song tuned the entire middle octave.

examples.text: 柠檬挞的香味飘满了整个咖啡角。
examples.trans: The aroma of lemon tart drifted through the entire café corner.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xīn xiān. Describes fresh fruit, fresh juice, or fresh herbs.

examples.text: 好。端上去之前，在上面撒这些新鲜绿香草。
examples.trans: Good. Before serving them, sprinkle these fresh green herbs on top.

examples.text: 闻闻看！热面包、热炒蛋，还有新鲜香草。
examples.trans: Smell that! Warm bread, hot scrambled eggs, and fresh herbs.

meanings.note: Pinyin: wú yán. Baking label meaning 'salt-free' (无盐黄油 'unsalted butter').

examples.text: 那是海盐咸黄油！甜果酱面包卷要无盐黄油！
examples.trans: That is sea-salt butter! Sweet jam rolls need unsalted butter!

examples.text: 烤柠檬蛋糕需要用新鲜的无盐黄油。
examples.trans: Baking lemon cake calls for fresh unsalted butter.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zǎo shang. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个早上 ('a morning').

examples.text: 早上好！请问，门锁了吗？
examples.trans: Good morning! Excuse me, is the door locked?

examples.text: 早上好。没锁，先把把手往上提，再推。
examples.trans: Good morning. Not locked; lift the handle up first, then push.

meanings.note: Pinyin: shì. Links two nouns (我是小晴); do NOT use simple 是 before plain adjectives like 好 or 忙.

examples.text: 啊，开了！谢谢。我是小晴，新来的前台。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Qing, the new receptionist.

examples.text: 有道理！这些是钥匙吗？
examples.trans: Fair enough! Are these the keys?

meanings.note: Pinyin: liàng jià. Combines 晾 ('air-dry/cool in open air') + 架 ('rack/stand'); in baking, wire racks that keep pastry bottoms crisp.

examples.text: 二十个酥脆的杏仁挞底已经在金属晾架上整整齐齐排好了。
examples.trans: Twenty crisp almond tart shells are already lined up neatly on the wire cooling rack.

examples.text: 刚烤好的面包要先放在晾架上散掉热气，表皮才会保持酥脆。
examples.trans: Freshly baked bread should rest on a cooling rack first to let off steam so the crust stays crisp.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xìng rén. Combines 杏 ('apricot/almond') + 仁 ('nut kernel').

examples.text: 小美端来了一盘刚出炉的温热杏仁饼干。
examples.trans: Mei brought over a plate of warm almond biscuits fresh from the oven.

examples.text: 用杏仁粉做的柠檬挞底吃起来特别香酥。
examples.trans: A lemon tart crust made with ground almonds tastes wonderfully crisp and nutty.

meanings.note: Pinyin: róu ruǎn. Near-synonym compound 柔 ('supple/gentle') + 软 ('soft'); used for well-kneaded dough, cushions, or fabrics.

examples.text: 发酵好的面团又光滑又柔软，轻轻按下去就会弹回来。
examples.trans: The risen dough is both smooth and soft, springing right back when pressed gently.

examples.text: 小美把受伤的脚踝放在两个柔软的枕头上休息。
examples.trans: Mei rested her injured ankle on two soft pillows.

meanings.note: Pinyin: níng méng. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个柠檬 ('a lemon').

examples.text: 他爷爷会切热柠檬蛋糕，上面撒一层白糖粉！
examples.trans: His grandfather sliced warm lemon cake with a dusting of powdered sugar on top!

examples.text: 啊！黄色柠檬糖霜——每个星期五我们俩都抢边角那一块！
examples.trans: Oh! Yellow lemon glaze—every single Friday the two of us fought over the corner piece!

meanings.note: Pinyin: níng méng zhī. Combines 柠檬 ('lemon') + 汁 ('squeezed juice').

examples.text: 碗里已经准备好了四个蛋黄、新鲜柠檬汁和三勺白糖。
examples.trans: Four egg yolks, fresh lemon juice, and three spoons of sugar are already waiting in the bowl.

examples.text: 挤几滴新鲜柠檬汁在热茶里，喝起来格外清爽。
examples.trans: Squeeze a few drops of fresh lemon juice into hot tea for a wonderfully bright taste.

meanings.note: Pinyin: níng méng jiàng. Combines 柠檬 ('lemon') + 酱 ('thick culinary spread/curd/jam'): rich custard cooked from lemon juice, egg yolks, sugar, and butter.

examples.text: 快看锅里，金黄的柠檬酱变得又浓稠又发亮！
examples.trans: Look in the pot—the golden lemon curd has turned so thick and glossy!

examples.text: 在酥脆的杏仁挞底里盛满温热的柠檬酱，香气扑鼻。
examples.trans: Filling the crisp almond tart shells with warm lemon curd sends up a mouthwatering aroma.

根.gloss: measure word for pipes, wires, sticks

meanings.en: measure word for pipes, wires, sticks
meanings.note: Pinyin: gēn. Counts long, thin rod-like or cord-like objects (一根水管 'a water pipe', 一根电线 'a wire').

examples.text: 先生，到了。小心碰头，这根木房梁比较低。
examples.trans: Here we are, sir. Mind your head—this wooden beam is fairly low.

examples.text: 老木匠换了一根新的铜水管。
examples.trans: The carpenter replaced it with a new copper water pipe.

meanings.note: Pinyin: cì. Standard verbal measure word counting how many times an action happens (一次 'once', 下次 'next time').

examples.text: 每次弹完琴，他都问为什么下雨天钢琴声音更暖。
examples.trans: Whenever I finished playing, he asked why the piano sounded warmer on rainy days.

examples.text: 说这话的人每隔三十秒就扒着窗帘偷看一次！
examples.trans: Says the man peeking through the window curtain every thirty seconds!

meanings.note: Pinyin: qì. Measure word (量词): 口 (kǒu), e.g. 一口气 ('a breath').

examples.text: 太松一口气了！志豪先生，给您银钥匙。
examples.trans: What a relief! Mr Zhihao, here is your silver key.

examples.text: 老陈，求你告诉我只是水管进了一点气！
examples.trans: Chen, please tell me it was just a tiny bit of air in the pipe!

meanings.note: Pinyin: nóng chóu. Combines 浓 ('rich/concentrated') + 稠 ('thick/dense'), describing custards, curds, sauces, or slow-simmered soups.

examples.text: 小火不停地搅动五分钟后，金黄的柠檬酱变得又浓稠又亮。
examples.trans: After five minutes of continuous stirring over low heat, the golden lemon curd turned thick and glossy.

examples.text: 红扁豆在热高汤里慢慢炖煮，汤汁变得越来越浓稠。
examples.trans: As the red lentils simmered gently in hot broth, the soup grew thicker and richer.

消肿.gloss: reduce swelling; go down in swelling

meanings.en: reduce swelling; go down in swelling
meanings.note: Pinyin: xiāo zhǒng. Separable verb-object compound 消 ('dissipate/subside') + 肿 ('swelling').

examples.text: 把脚垫高休息了一整晚，小美的脚踝已经消肿一半了。
examples.trans: After propping her foot up and resting all night, Mei's ankle swelling has already gone down by half.

examples.text: 扭伤脚踝以后先敷冰袋，能帮助更快消肿。
examples.trans: Applying an ice pack right after spraining an ankle helps the swelling go down faster.

meanings.note: Pinyin: qīng shuǎng. Combines 清 ('clear/fresh') + 爽 ('brisk/refreshing'), used for citrus aromas, morning air, or clean flavours.

examples.text: 闻闻这股清爽的柠檬热气，整个一楼都飘着香味！
examples.trans: Smell this waft of bright, refreshing lemon steam—the whole ground floor is filled with aroma!

examples.text: 雨后的院子空气格外清爽，连石板路都洗得干干净净。
examples.trans: After the rain, the air in the courtyard is extra crisp and refreshing, and even the flagstones are washed clean.

meanings.note: Pinyin: wēn. Describes lukewarm water or mild temperatures.

examples.text: 摸摸热水管——下面是温的，上面变凉了。
examples.trans: Feel the hot-water pipe—the bottom is warm, while the top is turning cool.

examples.text: 壶里的水还是温的，正好喝。
examples.trans: The water in the pot is still warm—just right to drink.

meanings.note: Pinyin: shī. Describes clothes, shoes, or streets wet from rain.

examples.text: 晚上好。不好意思，把干净地板弄湿了。
examples.trans: Good evening. Sorry for getting your clean floor wet.

examples.text: 因为湿木头百叶窗会柔化石板路传回来的回声……
examples.trans: Because wet wooden shutters soften the echo bouncing off the flagstones...

meanings.note: Pinyin: huǒ. Measure word (量词): 团, e.g. 一团火 ('a fire').

examples.text: 火苗亮了——稳稳的蓝火，正合适。
examples.trans: The flame is lit—steady blue fire, right as it should be.

examples.text: 炉子上的小火还开着。
examples.trans: The low flame on the stove is still on.

meanings.note: Pinyin: diǎnr. Colloquial erhua form of 一点 after adjectives and imperatives (小心点儿 'be a bit careful', 快点儿 'hurry a bit').

examples.text: 你们两个站在梯子上小心点儿！
examples.trans: Be careful up there on the ladder, you two!

examples.text: 夜里石板路有点滑，走的时候慢点儿。
examples.trans: The stone path is a bit slippery at night; walk a little slower.

meanings.note: Pinyin: rè. Describes hot tea, hot water, or warm weather.

examples.text: 第一条规矩：先喝热茶，再去开门。
examples.trans: Rule number one: drink hot tea first, then go answer the door.

examples.text: 因为好咖啡和热面包让人开心呀！
examples.trans: Because good coffee and warm bread make people happy!

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhǔ kāi. Resultative verb compound 煮 ('cook/heat liquid') + 开 ('reach a rolling boil').

examples.text: 做柠檬酱的时候要开小火慢慢搅，千万别让锅底煮开了！
examples.trans: When making lemon curd, stir gently over low heat and whatever you do, don't let the bottom of the pot boil!

examples.text: 等锅里的高汤煮开以后，再把火调小盖上锅盖慢炖。
examples.trans: Once the broth in the pot comes to a boil, turn the heat down low and cover the pot to simmer.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xiàn zài. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 现在这时候 ('this moment right now').

examples.text: 现在他的箱子还安全锁着呢。
examples.trans: For now, his suitcase stays safely locked up.

examples.text: 太好了！现在我想吃一顿丰盛的早餐。
examples.trans: Wonderful! Now I would like to eat a big breakfast.

related.gloss: this moment right now (measure word 个)

meanings.note: Pinyin: yòng. Works as main verb ('use a key') or preposition ('with/using').

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 别担心！用冰气泡水一擦，橙汁就掉。
examples.trans: Do not worry! Wipe it once with cold sparkling water and orange juice comes right out.

meanings.note: Pinyin: de. Links modifiers or owners to nouns (我的书 'my book', 安静的院子 'quiet courtyard').

examples.text: 啊，开了！谢谢。我是小晴，新来的前台。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Qing, the new receptionist.

examples.text: 纸本子？真的吗？
examples.trans: A paper notebook? Really?

meanings.note: Pinyin: gài. Used for stamping an official seal (盖印章) or putting on a lid.

examples.text: 邮递员刚让我签收的，上面盖着红色房产印章。
examples.trans: The postman just had me sign for it; it carries a red property-office stamp.

examples.text: 文件下面已经盖好了红色印章。
examples.trans: The red official seal has already been stamped at the bottom of the document.

meanings.note: Pinyin: kàn. Covers looking at something, reading silently, or visiting someone; add 见/到 for 'catch sight of'.

examples.text: 我要看预订本子，可是找不到我的眼镜了！
examples.trans: I need to read the booking ledger, yet I cannot find my glasses!

examples.text: 老板，看一下桌子后面的镜子。
examples.trans: Boss, take a look in the mirror behind the desk.

meanings.note: Evaluative verb phrase judging by outward appearance.

examples.text: 他和老朋友一边喝茶一边聊天，神情看起来非常轻松。
examples.trans: Chatting over tea with an old friend, he looked thoroughly relaxed.

examples.text: 这份策划案表面上看起来简单，执行起来却很有难度。
examples.trans: This proposal looks simple on paper yet takes real skill to execute.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhēn de. Used standalone ('Really?!' 真的吗？！) or before verbs as an emphatic adverb.

examples.text: 真的吗？！你真的把火车票改到星期六早上了？
examples.trans: Really?! Did you really move your train ticket to Saturday morning?

examples.text: 加了杏仁粉的柠檬挞真的特别香！
examples.trans: The lemon tart made with almond flour is truly fragrant!

meanings.note: Pinyin: wǎn. Measure word (量词): 只 (zhǐ), e.g. 一只碗 ('a bowl').

examples.text: 先生，给您干毛巾擦外套，还有一碗热汤。
examples.trans: Sir, here is a dry towel to wipe your coat, plus a bowl of hot soup.

examples.text: 热汤？在冷雨中走过来之后，这听起来太棒了。
examples.trans: Hot soup? After that cold walk in the rain, that sounds wonderful.

meanings.note: Pinyin: táng. Measure word (量词): 块 (kuài), e.g. 一块糖 ('a piece of candy / sugar cube').

examples.text: 请给我不加糖的红茶，再来一片热面包。
examples.trans: Black tea without added sugar, please, and one slice of warm bread.

examples.text: 太好了！请加牛奶和一点糖。
examples.trans: Wonderful! With milk and a little sugar, please.

related.gloss: a piece of candy / sugar cube (measure word 块)

罐.gloss: jar of; pot of; tin of

meanings.en: jar of; pot of; tin of
meanings.note: Pinyin: guàn. Serves both as a noun (罐子 'jar/crock') and as a measure word for jars or tins (两罐蜂蜜 'two jars of honey').

examples.text: 竹篮子里装着两罐沉甸甸的百花蜂蜜。
examples.trans: Packed inside the bamboo basket are two heavy jars of wildflower honey.

examples.text: 小美做了四小罐草莓果酱放在厨房架子上。
examples.trans: Mei made four small jars of strawberry jam and set them on the kitchen shelf.

股.gloss: waft; puff; stream (measure word for scents, steam, or currents)

meanings.en: waft; puff; stream (measure word for scents, steam, or currents)
meanings.note: Pinyin: gǔ. Classifier for invisible currents of air, fragrance, steam, or energy (这股柠檬热气 'this waft of lemon steam', 一股香味 'a waft of fragrance').

examples.text: 闻闻这股清爽的柠檬热气，整个一楼都是甜点香味！
examples.trans: Smell this bright, refreshing waft of lemon steam—the whole ground floor is filled with pastry aroma!

examples.text: 刚打开烤箱门，一股麦香和黄油香就扑面而来。
examples.trans: The moment the oven door opened, a rich waft of wheat and butter fragrance greeted us.

meanings.note: Pinyin: jiǎo huái. Combines 脚 ('foot') + 踝 ('ankle joint'); measure word: 只 (zhī) or 个 (gè).

examples.text: 志鹏关心地问：“小美，今天早上你的脚踝感觉怎么样？”
examples.trans: Peng asked warmly, 'Mei, how does your ankle feel this morning?'

examples.text: 休息了一天半以后，小美扭伤的脚踝已经消肿，到星期五就能站起来了。
examples.trans: After a day and a half of rest, Mei's sprained ankle has gone down in swelling and she will be able to stand by Friday.

meanings.note: Pinyin: dàn huáng. Combines 蛋 ('egg') + 黄 ('yellow yolk'); contrasts with 蛋白/蛋清 ('egg white'); measure word: 个 (gè).

examples.text: 小晴在碗里准备好了四个新鲜蛋黄、柠檬汁和三勺白糖。
examples.trans: Qing had four fresh egg yolks, lemon juice, and three spoons of sugar ready in the bowl.

examples.text: 做柠檬酱只用蛋黄不用蛋白，这样熬出来的酱才会金黄浓稠。
examples.trans: Lemon curd is made with egg yolks rather than whites so that the cooked curd turns out golden and rich.

meanings.note: Pinyin: jiàn. Appears in farewells (再见, 明天见) and as result complement of perception (看见, 听见).

examples.text: 晚安，小晴。明天早餐见。
examples.trans: Good night, Qing. See you at breakfast tomorrow.

examples.text: 老陈，听得见吗？我刚经过绿药店！
examples.trans: Chen, can you hear me? I just passed the green pharmacy!

meanings.note: Pinyin: ràng. Everyday causative/polite-offer verb (让我看看 'let me have a look').

examples.text: 因为好咖啡和热面包让人开心呀！
examples.trans: Because good coffee and warm bread make people happy!

examples.text: 宋老师，让我来给您倒新鲜橙汁！
examples.trans: Teacher Song, allow me to pour fresh orange juice for you!

meanings.note: Pinyin: shuō. Most common verb of speaking.

examples.text: 谁也别说出去！门铃响的时候要微笑。
examples.trans: Do not tell anyone! Smile warmly when the bell rings.

examples.text: 我还没喝早咖啡呢，千万别说急事！
examples.trans: I have not had my morning coffee yet; please do not say emergency!

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhuàn. Read zhuàn for spinning wheels or quick wits (脑子转得快 'mind works fast').

examples.text: 脑子转得快，小晴。志豪每星期都读城市建筑规定。
examples.trans: Quick thinking, Qing. Hao reads city building rules every single week.

examples.text: 风一吹，纸风车就飞快地转起来。
examples.trans: When the breeze blows, the paper pinwheel spins fast.

meanings.en: and also; in addition; still have
meanings.note: Pinyin: hái yǒu. Adds another item to a list ('plus…').

examples.text: 只有裙子、乐谱，还有我最喜欢的茶杯！
examples.trans: Only dresses, sheet music, and my favourite teacup!

examples.text: 两双棕色大男鞋，还有灰色毛衣。
examples.trans: Two pairs of big brown men's shoes, plus grey sweaters.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhè. Proximal demonstrative; pairs with a measure word before nouns (这个 'this one', 这间房 'this room').

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 小美跟这条街上所有人说话都像老朋友。
examples.trans: Mei talks to everyone on this street like old friends.

meanings.note: Pinyin: jìn. Movement into an enclosed space (请进 'come in!', 倒进 'pour into').

examples.text: 小晴，把热水倒进茶壶里，他们来了！
examples.trans: Qing, pour the hot water into the teapot—here they come!

examples.text: 没有啊，周经理，南方来的夫妻一小时前住进六号房了。
examples.trans: No, Manager Zhou, the couple from the south checked into room six an hour ago.

进去.gloss: go in; seep in (away from speaker)

meanings.en: go in; seep in (away from speaker)
meanings.note: Pinyin: jìn qù. Directional complement 进 ('enter') + 去 ('away from speaker'), e.g. 渗进去 ('seep in').

examples.text: 等机油渗进去十秒钟，我们再一起拉窗板。
examples.trans: Give the oil ten seconds to seep in, then let's pull the shutter together.

examples.text: 九号房已经擦干净了，快进去看看有多亮堂吧！
examples.trans: Room Nine is all wiped clean—go on in and see how bright it is!

meanings.note: Pinyin: dōu. Summarizes everything BEFORE it and always stands directly before the verb/adjective (我们都喜欢).

examples.text: 谢谢！我们平时都直接叫名字吗？
examples.trans: Thank you! Do we usually just call each other by name here?

examples.text: 小美跟这条街上所有人说话都像老朋友。
examples.trans: Mei talks to everyone on this street like old friends.

meanings.note: Pinyin: sū cuì. Combines 酥 ('flaky/short/tender-crisp') + 脆 ('crunchy/crisp'), the ideal texture for tart shells, biscuits, and bread crusts.

examples.text: 二十个金黄酥脆的杏仁挞底已经在晾架上排好了。
examples.trans: Twenty golden, crisp and flaky almond tart shells are already lined up on the cooling rack.

examples.text: 刚出炉的面包外皮酥脆，里面却非常柔软。
examples.trans: Fresh from the oven, the bread has a crisp, flaky crust while staying soft inside.

meanings.note: Pinyin: lǐ. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 里面 ('the inside').

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 在您的外套口袋里吗？
examples.trans: Are they in your coat pocket?

meanings.note: Pinyin: jīn huáng. Praises freshly baked pastry crusts.

examples.text: 正在架子上放凉呢——金黄外皮配甜柠檬糖霜！
examples.trans: Cooling on the rack right now—golden crust with sweet lemon glaze!

examples.text: 刚烤出来的面包卷外皮一片金黄。
examples.trans: Freshly baked bread rolls came out golden-brown.

meanings.note: Pinyin: guō dǐ. Combines 锅 ('pot/pan') + 底 ('bottom/base').

examples.text: 熬柠檬酱的时候要用木勺贴着锅底不停地搅，千万别让锅底煮开了。
examples.trans: When cooking lemon curd, stir continuously along the bottom of the pot with a wooden spoon so it never boils.

examples.text: 浓汤很容易粘在锅底，所以一定要开小火慢慢炖。
examples.trans: Thick soup catches easily on the bottom of the pot, so be sure to simmer it gently over low heat.

meanings.note: Pinyin: wén wen. Friendly reduplication of 闻.

examples.text: 闻闻看！热面包、热炒蛋，还有新鲜香草。
examples.trans: Smell that! Warm bread, hot scrambled eggs, and fresh herbs.

examples.text: 来闻闻这壶刚泡好的薄荷茶香不香！
examples.trans: Come smell how fragrant this freshly steeped pot of mint tea is!

meanings.note: Pinyin: miàn bāo fáng. Combines 面包 ('bread') + 房 ('house/workshop/room'); measure word: 家 (jiā) or 间 (jiān).

examples.text: 小美笑着对志鹏和小晴说：“两位徒弟，我的面包房交给你们放心了！”
examples.trans: Mei smiled at Peng and Qing and said, 'Apprentices, I can rest easy leaving my bakery in your hands!'

examples.text: 每天早上六点，一楼的面包房就会飘出烤面包和黄油的香气。
examples.trans: Every morning at six o'clock, the aroma of baking bread and butter drifts from the ground-floor bakery.

meanings.note: Pinyin: miàn tuán. Measure word (量词): 团, e.g. 一团面团 ('a ball of dough').

examples.text: 还好烤箱里的面团已经放进去了。
examples.trans: My dough is already in the oven, at least.

examples.text: 揉好的面团放在温暖的地方醒发一小时。
examples.trans: Set the kneaded dough in a warm spot to rise for an hour.

related.gloss: a ball of dough (measure word 团)

meanings.note: Pinyin: xiāng wèi. Measure word (量词): 股, e.g. 一股香味 ('a waft of aroma').

examples.text: 早上好！在楼上就闻到暖暖的肉桂香味了！
examples.trans: Good morning! All the way upstairs I smelled warm cinnamon!

examples.text: 热黄油和肉桂的香味飘到了院子里。
examples.trans: The aroma of warm butter and cinnamon drifted out into the courtyard.

related.gloss: a waft of aroma (measure word 股)

meanings.note: Pinyin: mǎ shàng. Literally 'on horseback'—everyday word for 'right now!'.

examples.text: 您先坐下，别着急，我们马上看行李牌。
examples.trans: Please sit down first and do not worry; we will check the luggage tag right away.

examples.text: 小晴，马上给火车站失物处打电话。
examples.trans: Qing, call the train station lost-and-found office right away.

meanings.note: Pinyin: huáng yóu. Measure word (量词): 块 (kuài), e.g. 一块黄油 ('a block of butter').

examples.text: 只有一点点牛奶、两个鸡蛋，一点黄油都没有！
examples.trans: Only a tiny bit of milk, two eggs, and no butter at all!

examples.text: 三瓶牛奶、二十个鸡蛋、黄油、奶酪和红苹果！
examples.trans: Three bottles of milk, twenty eggs, butter, cheese, and red apples!

related.gloss: a block of butter (measure word 块)
